value: This randomized controlled trial investigated how medication labeling influences the efficacy of both placebo and active drug (rizatriptan) in 66 patients with episodic migraine. Participants received either placebo or Maxalt under three information conditions: labeled as placebo, as Maxalt or placebo, or as Maxalt, across six distinct migraine attacks. Results showed that while Maxalt was superior to placebo, the progressive increase in 'positive' labeling incrementally boosted the efficacy of both placebo and Maxalt. Notably, placebo labeled as Maxalt was as effective as Maxalt labeled as placebo, and even open-label placebo outperformed no treatment, with placebo effects accounting for over 50% of the drug effect relative to no treatment. These findings underscore the substantial impact of patient information and the treatment ritual on therapeutic outcomes, emphasizing their critical role in patient care for conditions like migraine.
